"title": "Uniﬁcation of the phonon mode behaviour in semiconductor alloys",
"authors": "O. Pag`es, M. Kassem, A. Chaﬁ, A. Nassour, S. Doyen and A. V. Postnikov",
"field_subfield": "Condensed matter physics / materials science (vibrational spectroscopy of semiconductor alloys)",
"type_of_paper": "Theoretical/computational study with literature data analysis and ab initio calculations",
"executive_summary": "This paper concludes a series of systematic re-examinations of Raman and infrared (IR) spectra of representative semiconductor alloys, namely In1−xGaxAs (1-bond→1-mode), In1−xGaxP (modified 2-mode) and ZnTe1−xSex (traditionally classified as 2-bond→1-mode). The authors challenge the traditionally admitted classification of phonon mode behaviour, which is based on the virtual crystal approximation (VCA) and the modified-random-element-isodisplacement (MREI) model. They argue that the VCA misses the essence of phonon behaviour in alloys because it treats the alloy at the macroscopic scale as a continuum, whereas the bond force constant K is sensitive to local bond distortions at the mesoscopic scale. The central claim is that ZnTe1−xSex obeys the same phonon mode behaviour as In1−xGaxAs and In1−xGaxP, namely a universal percolation-type behaviour of 1-bond→2-mode. The authors propose a three-oscillator [1 (Zn-Te), 2 (Zn-Se)] version of the percolation model, supported by extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) data and home-made ab initio phonon calculations. The percolation model requires two adjustable parameters per bond, i.e. the frequency of the impurity mode ωimp plus the splitting ∆ between like TO modes in the dilute limit. The ωimp values were estimated by relying on thorough EXAFS measurements of bond length in ZnTeSe, and the shift of an impurity mode with respect to the TO mode in the pure crystal was inferred from the related difference in bond length δ via the TO mode Gr¨uneisen parameter γ in the pure crystal. For the Zn-Te (Zn-Se) bond, δ and γ are 2.480–2.452 Å (2.600–2.643 Å) and 1.4 (1.7), according to refs. 15 and 16, respectively. The (ωimp, ∆) values for the Zn-Te and Zn-Se bonds are (∼189 cm−1, ∼0 cm−1) and (∼195 cm−1, ∼8 cm−1), respectively. The agreement between the TO (thick lines) / LO (thin lines) theoretical curves and the data is rather good, in spite of the simplicity of our model. The authors also provide independent ab initio insight into the TO density of states (TO-DOS) at the zone-center (ZC), that compares directly to the Raman signal, in a fully-relaxed 32-atom supercell at the representative composition x∼0.5. They apply the plane-wave pseudopotential method within the density functional theory and the local density approximation (LDA), and a linear response technique. The ZC TO-DOS obtained per atom for uniformly-damped Zn, Se and Te oscillators (∼10 cm−1) show three equidistant oscillators spaced by ∼10 cm−1, with similar strengths, i.e. a ZnTe-like below two ZnSe-like ones. A slight overall blue-shift of the ZC TO-DOS with respect to the corresponding Raman lineshape (∼20 cm−1) is due to a well-known overbinding in LDA. The authors show that ZnTeSe obeys the 1-bond→2-phonon percolation model, as InGaAs and InGaP do, which leads to unification of the traditional MREI-VCA/Elliott-CPA classification into a single class covered by the percolation model. They emphasize that even those ideally-disordered systems that are the usual SC alloys cannot escape a description of some of their very basic physical properties via a percolation concept. On the practical side, this work reveals that vibrational spectroscopies provide natural insight (non destructive and contactless) into the alloy disorder at the unusual mesoscopic scale, which offers an attractive perspective for the study of the long scale (self-) organization in alloys. The authors acknowledge support from the IFCPAR (N◦3204-1) and the CINES (N◦pli2623).",

summary.title: Uniﬁcation of the phonon mode behaviour in semiconductor alloys
summary.authors: O. Pag`es, M. Kassem, A. Chaﬁ, A. Nassour, S. Doyen and A. V. Postnikov
summary.field_subfield: Condensed matter physics / materials science (vibrational spectroscopy of semiconductor alloys)
summary.type_of_paper: Theoretical/computational study with literature data analysis and ab initio calculations
summary.executive_summary: This paper concludes a series of systematic re-examinations of Raman and infrared (IR) spectra of representative semiconductor alloys, namely In1−xGaxAs (1-bond→1-mode), In1−xGaxP (modified 2-mode) and ZnTe1−xSex (traditionally classified as 2-bond→1-mode). The authors challenge the traditionally admitted classification of phonon mode behaviour, which is based on the virtual crystal approximation (VCA) and the modified-random-element-isodisplacement (MREI) model. They argue that the VCA misses the essence of phonon behaviour in alloys because it treats the alloy at the macroscopic scale as a continuum, whereas the bond force constant K is sensitive to local bond distortions at the mesoscopic scale. The central claim is that ZnTe1−xSex obeys the same phonon mode behaviour as In1−xGaxAs and In1−xGaxP, namely a universal percolation-type behaviour of 1-bond→2-mode. The authors propose a three-oscillator [1 (Zn-Te), 2 (Zn-Se)] version of the percolation model, supported by extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) data and home-made ab initio phonon calculations. The percolation model requires two adjustable parameters per bond, i.e. the frequency of the impurity mode ωimp plus the splitting ∆ between like TO modes in the dilute limit. The ωimp values were estimated by relying on thorough EXAFS measurements of bond length in ZnTeSe, and the shift of an impurity mode with respect to the TO mode in the pure crystal was inferred from the related difference in bond length δ via the TO mode Gr¨uneisen parameter γ in the pure crystal. For the Zn-Te (Zn-Se) bond, δ and γ are 2.480–2.452 Å (2.600–2.643 Å) and 1.4 (1.7), according to refs. 15 and 16, respectively. The (ωimp, ∆) values for the Zn-Te and Zn-Se bonds are (∼189 cm−1, ∼0 cm−1) and (∼195 cm−1, ∼8 cm−1), respectively. The agreement between the TO (thick lines) / LO (thin lines) theoretical curves and the data is rather good, in spite of the simplicity of our model. The authors also provide independent ab initio insight into the TO density of states (TO-DOS) at the zone-center (ZC), that compares directly to the Raman signal, in a fully-relaxed 32-atom supercell at the representative composition x∼0.5. They apply the plane-wave pseudopotential method within the density functional theory and the local density approximation (LDA), and a linear response technique. The ZC TO-DOS obtained per atom for uniformly-damped Zn, Se and Te oscillators (∼10 cm−1) show three equidistant oscillators spaced by ∼10 cm−1, with similar strengths, i.e. a ZnTe-like below two ZnSe-like ones. A slight overall blue-shift of the ZC TO-DOS with respect to the corresponding Raman lineshape (∼20 cm−1) is due to a well-known overbinding in LDA. The authors show that ZnTeSe obeys the 1-bond→2-phonon percolation model, as InGaAs and InGaP do, which leads to unification of the traditional MREI-VCA/Elliott-CPA classification into a single class covered by the percolation model. They emphasize that even those ideally-disordered systems that are the usual SC alloys cannot escape a description of some of their very basic physical properties via a percolation concept. On the practical side, this work reveals that vibrational spectroscopies provide natural insight (non destructive and contactless) into the alloy disorder at the unusual mesoscopic scale, which offers an attractive perspective for the study of the long scale (self-) organization in alloys. The authors acknowledge support from the IFCPAR (N◦3204-1) and the CINES (N◦pli2623).

On the practical side, this work reveals that vibrational spectroscopies provide natural insight (non destructive and contactless) into the alloy disorder at the unusual mesoscopic scale, which offers an attractive perspective for the study of the long scale (self-) organization in alloys. The authors acknowledge support from the IFCPAR (N◦3204-1) and the CINES (N◦pli2623).

Research Context
The study concludes a series of systematic re-examinations of the Raman/Infrared spectra of representative semiconductor alloys. The traditionally admitted classification is based on the virtual crystal approximation (VCA). The VCA treats the alloy at the macroscopic scale as a continuum, with each atom A surrounded by four virtual B1−xCx atoms. The physical properties are accordingly averaged, and no singularity is expected in their dependence on x. The key issue regarding mixtures is how to handle the substitutional disorder. A percolation-based approach was developed at the mesoscopic scale, with the central notion being the volume fraction of each constituent. Singularities in the physical properties are expected at the percolation thresholds, at which compositions the minor constituents coalesce into a continuum. The VCA seems sufficient, in first approximation, for ideally-disordered mixtures that are usual semiconductor AB1−xCx alloys. The bond force constant K is sensitive to the bond distortion required to accommodate the mismatch in the A-B and A-C bond lengths. The VCA for K leads to a 1-bond→1-mode TO behaviour, as accounted for by the MREI model. The Elliott et al. criterion within the coherent potential approximation (CPA) predicts type (ii) when the A-B and A-C optical bands overlap in the alloy. The MREI-VCA (experimental) and Elliott-CPA (theoretical) classifications were found to be remarkably consistent, except for InGaP. The apparent anomalies in InGa(As,P) could be explained within a 1-bond→2-mode percolation model. The perspective is a change of paradigm regarding the way to describe phonons in alloys.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The study investigates whether the percolation scheme for InGa(As,P) is fortuitous or reflects a deeper universal reality. The hypothesis is that ZnTeSe obeys the same phonon mode behaviour as InGaAs and InGaP, namely a universal percolation-type behaviour of 1-bond→2-mode. The lattice mismatch in ZnTeSe is similar to that of InGa(As,P), i.e. ∼7%, so that similar lattice distortions can be expected. The hypothesis is that a InGaP-like version of the percolation model should apply to ZnTeSe. The VCA misses the essence of the phonon behaviour in alloys, and the proper understanding of TO phonons requires insight into the topologies of the (B,C)-substituting species. The hypothesis is that the traditional MREI-VCA/Elliott-CPA classification has no raison d'ˆetre, and that all these alloys belong to a single percolation class. The predicted outcome is that ZnTeSe exhibits three equally spaced TO modes in the range 180–200 cm−1, that blue-shift when the Se content increases. The predicted outcome is that the percolation schemes for InGaAs, InGaP and ZnTeSe are analogous, indicating that the traditional classification has no raison d'ˆetre. The predicted outcome is that the percolation schemes are consistent with the MREI-VCA classification, as a matter of regrouping close individual/double TO branches. The predicted outcome is that vibrational spectroscopies provide natural insight into the alloy disorder at the unusual mesoscopic scale.

Methodological Details
The study focuses on the bond force constant K in SC alloys, which is sensitive to the bond distortion required to accommodate the mismatch in the A-B and A-C bond lengths. K is routinely probed by Raman and Infrared (IR) spectroscopies, via the frequency of the transverse optical (TO) phonon. The MREI-VCA model requires only one adjustable parameter per bond, i.e. the frequency of the impurity mode ωimp. The MREI-VCA supports a classification of the TO-Raman/IR data in terms of 2-mode (pure 1-bond→1-mode), mixed-mode (2-bond→1-mode) and dominant-plus-minor mixed-modes (modified-2-mode). Representative systems are In1−xGaxAs, ZnTe1−xSex and In1−xGaxP, respectively. The percolation model requires two adjustable parameters per bond, i.e. ωimp plus the splitting ∆ between like TO modes in the dilute limit. The ωimp values were estimated by relying on thorough extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) measurements of bond length in ZnTeSe. The shift of an impurity mode with respect to the TO mode in the pure crystal was inferred from the related difference in bond length δ via the TO mode Gr¨uneisen parameter γ in the pure crystal. For the Zn-Te (Zn-Se) bond, δ and γ are 2.480–2.452 Å (2.600–2.643 Å) and 1.4 (1.7), according to refs. 15 and 16, respectively. The (ωimp, ∆) values for the Zn-Te and Zn-Se bonds are (∼189 cm−1, ∼0 cm−1) and (∼195 cm−1, ∼8 cm−1), respectively. The authors use the generic expression of the Raman cross section given by Eq. (1) in ref. 9, in a form restricted to the second member it gives access to the TO modes; in full it provides the LO modes. The authors use a classical form of the dielectric function, generalized to three harmonic oscillators. The authors take Zn-Se and Zn-Te phonon dampings that scale like in pure crystals, i.e. 3:1, as inferred from the full widths at half maximum of the LO Raman lines. The remaining (CF−H, ϵ∞, TO–LO) values for the pure ZnSe and ZnTe crystals are (−0.56, 5.75, 206–252 cm−1) and (−0.32, 7.20, 176–206 cm−1), respectively. The authors use small dampings for the Zn-Te (1 cm−1) and Zn-Se (3 cm−1) modes, for a clear overview of the whole collection of oscillators. The authors provide independent ab initio insight into the TO density of states (TO-DOS) at the zone-center (ZC), in a fully-relaxed 32-atom supercell at the representative composition x∼0.5. The authors apply the plane-wave pseudopotential method within the density functional theory and the local density approximation (LDA), and a linear response technique. The authors use 64-atom supercells, that are well-converged in size for such purpose. The authors use a supercell containing a single impurity (∼3% imp.) to access ωimp. The authors use a supercell containing two neighbouring substitutional impurities to access ∆. The systematic error due to LDA is thus eliminated, and the theoretical and experimental (ωimp, ∆) values agree within ∼5%. The theoretical and experimental (ωimp, ∆) values for random InGaAs, InGaP and ZnTeSe, and also (Zn,Be)-chalcogenides, agree within ∼5%. The Se and Te atoms are equally distributed over all substituting planes, as expected in a random alloy. The ZC TO-DOS obtained per atom for uniformly-damped Zn, Se and Te oscillators (∼10 cm−1) show three equidistant oscillators spaced by ∼10 cm−1. A slight overall blue-shift of the ZC TO-DOS with respect to the corresponding Raman lineshape (∼20 cm−1) is due to a well-known overbinding in LDA.

Procedures And Architectures
The authors propose a three-oscillator [1 (Zn-Te), 2 (Zn-Se)] version of the percolation model, with a unique TOZn−Te branch below a well-resolved Zn-Se TO double-branch. Bonds are longer (shorter) in environments rich of the shorter (longer) bonds, which reduces (enlarges) the TO frequency. The middle and upper TO branches are due to Zn-Se vibrations in the Se- and Te-rich regions, accordingly labelled as TOSeZn−Se and TOTeZn−Se. The lower set of TO data is attached to the limit (x∼0,1) Zn-Te frequencies at its two ends, indicating an apparent 1-bond→1-mode MREI behaviour for the Zn-Te bond, which comes to ∆Zn−Te ∼0 cm−1. The remaining sets of TO data share quasi-symmetrically on each side of the limit Zn-Se frequencies, indicating a well-resolved 1-bond→2-mode type behaviour for the Zn-Se bond. This was adjusted to ∼8 cm−1 by fitting a rescaled-MREI curve to the data in the continuum regime of the dominant TOSeZn−Se branch at large Se content. The remaining pieces of the Zn-Se double-branch were directly inferred, see Methods. The agreement between the TO (thick lines) / LO (thin lines) theoretical curves and the data is rather good, in spite of the simplicity of our model. Slight discrepancy exists with respect to the TOTeZn−Se branch in the Te-dilute limit, where the mode becomes weak and hard to detect. The authors re-assign the presumed unique TO mode in the Raman/IR spectra of ZnTeSe as the sum of close TOZn−Te and TOSeZn−Se modes. The two modes exhibit antagonist strength variations when the composition changes, and have similar heights at ∼70% Se, consistently with experimental observations. The authors use the percolation picture, in which the alloy is described at the mesoscopic scale as a composite, with the result of different local bond distortions. The percolation schemes for InGaAs, InGaP and ZnTeSe are schematically reproduced in Fig. 4, and there is an obvious analogy between the three schemes. In both InGaAs and InGaP, the impurity modes stay out of the parent TO-LO bands, so that the Ga- and In-related TO-LO bands in the alloy do not overlap. In contrast the Zn-Se and Zn-Te TO-LO bands do overlap in ZnTeSe, which is consistent with the Elliott-CPA classification of InGa(As,P) and ZnTeSe as types (i) and (ii), respectively. The usual terminology of individual modes [(i), Fig. 4a], dominant-plus-minor modes [(iii), Fig. 4b] and mixed-mode [(ii), Fig. 4c] comes out naturally. The authors emphasize that the TO and LO modes behave differently in an alloy, and that the actual 1-bond→2-mode behaviour visible in the TO symmetry is literally rubbed out in the LO symmetry. The authors show that ZnTeSe obeys the 1-bond→2-phonon percolation model, as InGaAs and InGaP do. This leads to unification of the traditional MREI-VCA/Elliott-CPA classification into a single class covered by the percolation model.

Key Results
The data indicate three equally spaced TO modes in the range 180–200 cm−1, that blue-shift when the Se content increases. The (ωimp, ∆) values for the Zn-Te and Zn-Se bonds are (∼189 cm−1, ∼0 cm−1) and (∼195 cm−1, ∼8 cm−1), respectively. The agreement between the TO (thick lines) / LO (thin lines) theoretical curves and the data is rather good, in spite of the simplicity of our model. Slight discrepancy exists with respect to the TOTeZn−Se branch in the Te-dilute limit, where the mode becomes weak and hard to detect. As expected, three equidistant oscillators spaced by ∼10 cm−1, with similar strengths, i.e. a ZnTe-like below two ZnSe-like ones, show up. The two modes exhibit antagonist strength variations when the composition changes, and have similar heights at ∼70% Se, consistently with experimental observations. The LO-TO inverted splitting is large at intermediate composition, and further increases with the Te content, as evidenced by Burlakov et al. (ref. 6). There is an obvious analogy between the three schemes, indicating that the traditional MREI-VCA/Elliott-CPA classification has, in fact, no raison d'ˆetre. The resulting three-mode TO and LO Raman lineshapes are shown in Fig. 3. In a multi-wave system, such as an alloy, the electric field ⃗E is well-known to act as a carrier of coherence, that makes LO modes a complicated issue. The individual LOZn−Te, LOSeZn−Se and LOTeZn−Se modes do ⃗E-couple strongly, with the result that the available oscillator strength is almost fully channelled into a 'giant' LO+ mode at high frequency. Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution: The authors unify the phonon mode behaviour of InGaAs, InGaP and ZnTeSe under a single percolation model (1-bond→2-mode), challenging the traditional MREI-VCA/Elliott-CPA classification. 2. The strongest evidence: The three-oscillator [1 Zn-Te, 2 Zn-Se] percolation model fits the TO/LO Raman lineshapes and the ab initio TO-DOS, with the theoretical and experimental (ωimp, ∆) values agreeing within ∼5%. 3. The future path: The percolation concept offers a natural insight into the alloy disorder at the unusual mesoscopic scale, with potential interest for the study of the long scale (self-) organization in alloys.
